sentences.text: Pleistorallus flemingi was an extinct bird belonging to the rail family.
This bird was a large and stout rail roughly the same size as the living takahē.
Trevor Worthy described the species in 1997 based on fossils found near Marton in New Zealand's North Island.
The genus Pleistorallus is classified within the family Rallidae.
The animal lived in New Zealand during the Middle Pleistocene, approximately one million years ago.
Fossils of this genus date from the Gelasian to the Late Pleistocene, between 2.58 and 0.0117 million years ago.
